actions.justification: Mandatory action - assess vital signs first to establish baseline and identify any abnormalities in this pregnant patient.
Determine the primary reason for presentation to guide further workup and management in this pregnant patient.
General status assessment to evaluate overall condition and identify any acute distress or concerning findings.
Patient is pregnant - cardiovascular assessment is essential to evaluate hemodynamic status and identify any cardiac concerns in the context of pregnancy.
Abdominal assessment is critical in a pregnant patient to evaluate uterine status, fetal well-being, and identify any obstetric or abdominal pathology.
Mental status assessment helps identify any neurological compromise or altered consciousness relevant to the clinical presentation.
Neurological assessment is part of a complete systematic evaluation, particularly important in pregnancy where conditions like eclampsia can present with neurological symptoms.
Hydration status assessment is important in pregnancy to evaluate for dehydration, which is common and clinically significant in pregnant patients.
Assessing for infection source is relevant in pregnancy as pregnant patients are at increased risk for infections (e.g., UTI, chorioamnionitis) that may not always present with fever initially.
Comprehensive patient assessment to consolidate findings from individual system assessments and establish working diagnosis for this pregnant patient.
Pain assessment is important in a pregnant patient to identify obstetric or other causes requiring urgent intervention.
Evaluate for organ dysfunction which may indicate serious conditions such as preeclampsia, HELLP syndrome, or sepsis in a pregnant patient.
Respiratory assessment is important in pregnancy as physiological changes affect respiratory function; this has not yet been completed.
Monitoring urine output is critical in pregnancy to assess renal perfusion and detect conditions such as preeclampsia or acute kidney injury.
Skin assessment can reveal signs of conditions relevant to pregnancy (e.g., rashes, edema, jaundice) that may guide diagnosis.
Complete the comprehensive physical assessment with musculoskeletal evaluation, important for a pregnant patient to assess for any musculoskeletal complaints contributing to presentation.
Patient has pregnancy as a comorbidity; obstetrics/maternal-fetal medicine specialist consultation is indicated to guide safe management and ensure fetal wellbeing.
Baseline renal function (eGFR) is important in pregnancy to detect preeclampsia, renal compromise, or guide medication dosing safely.
Assess neurological deficit severity using NIHSS, relevant given pregnancy comorbidity and need to rule out neurological conditions such as stroke or eclampsia-related neurological compromise.
Establishing IV access is a foundational step for a pregnant patient to enable fluid administration, medication delivery, and lab draws as workup proceeds.

Given the patient is pregnant and has presented requiring full assessment, hospital admission is indicated to ensure monitoring of both mother and fetus while the clinical syndrome is further clarified.
